question: For every registered natural-experiment design (wave 1 and wave 2), what is the smallest effect it could detect with 80% power, how often does it claim an effect when there is none, and how often does a correct design with no effect pass its own pre-trend and placebo-date checks?
relation_to_wave_1: Wave 1 reported four failures without saying whether any design could have succeeded. A null from an underpowered design and a failed diagnostic from a design whose checks reject correct designs half the time mean different things; this study measures both for each design, and records a design that cannot detect a plausible effect as such.

treatment.definition: none: synthetic panels carry no effect. Each covered design's real treatment timing (cohorts), units, observed unit-periods, strata and clusters are kept exactly

units.definition: the real primary-outcome panel of each covered design, rebuilt from its pinned inputs by its own code; wave-1 panels must reproduce the digests their published results recorded

controls.control_group: each design's own registered comparison group

primary.label: minimum detectable effect at 80% power, two-sided alpha 0.05, for a homogeneous additive effect on the post-period cells
primary.unit: outcome units (log points; Spearman for the ranking test)

secondary.label: share of synthetic null panels in which the design's overall ATT test rejects at 0.05 (negative control: the test's real size)
share of null panels passing the pre-trend Wald test and the placebo-date test (each at 0.05) and both

estimator.estimand: operating characteristics of each registered design
estimator.calibration: on each real panel's untreated cells only (never-treated units; treated units before g - anticipation): residuals after unit and stratum-by-period means, then first differences (so unit effects never enter). AR(1) coefficient rho from the autocorrelation of within-cluster differenced residuals (corr = -(1 - rho)/2, bounded to [-0.9, 0.98]); unit-specific innovation variances shrunk toward the pooled value with 5 pseudo-observations; a cluster-by-period innovation variance from the between-unit variation of cluster-period means, with the same rho. No post-treatment outcome of a treated unit enters calibration.
estimator.simulation: outcome_it = AR(1)_i(t) + AR(1)_cluster(i)(t) on exactly the real observed cells; each replication runs the design's registered primary estimator (bootstrap off, analytic clustered SE) and its placebo-date test. Placebo-unit and placebo-cluster tests are not simulated (each is itself a 100-replication simulation).
estimator.power: the estimators are linear in the outcomes, so a homogeneous additive effect delta on the treated post-period cells shifts the estimate by exactly delta with an unchanged SE: power(delta) = share of null draws with |att + delta| / se > 1.96, and MDE = smallest |delta| (the larger of the increase and decrease directions) with power >= 0.8
estimator.calibration_check: the mean simulated SE is compared with the real panel's analytic SE; if their ratio is outside [0.67, 1.5] the calibration is declared failed and the reported MDE is the analytic 2.80 x real SE instead of the simulated one. Both are always reported.
estimator.ranking_design: for the wave-1 exposure ranking test: synthetic studies resample the 42 held-out storms' centred per-storm Spearman differences (exposure minus naive) with replacement and add delta; the one-sided sign-flip test is applied in its normal approximation; MDE by bisection at 80% power

inference.note: Monte Carlo error with 200 draws is about +/-3 percentage points on a rejection rate near 0.8

placebo_tests.none: the synthetic null panels are the negative control

designs.plausible_rationale: 1% of county covered employment averaged over five years after a county's first major disaster. Studies of US hurricanes and large disasters find county employment or earnings effects of roughly 0.5-5% (e.g. Belasen and Polachek 2008 on Florida hurricanes; Strobl 2011); most first declarations are for moderate events, so 1% is a plausible average, not an upper bound.

Import demand elasticities with respect to tariff-inclusive prices of about 2-5 (Fajgelbaum et al. 2020; Caliendo and Parro 2015) imply 4-10% lower imports for a 2 pp increase and more for the typical increase in the sample; 5% is a conservative plausible effect.

designs.reason: No panel exists: the design stopped at its feasibility gate (7 of 19,776 designated parties map to a 13F security; gate 30) and never read an outcome. With 7 treated securities no staggered design is estimable, so it cannot detect any effect; recorded as such.

designs.plausible_rationale: An improvement of 0.05 in the mean per-storm Spearman correlation over distance to track would be a meaningful ranking gain; the wave-1 observed difference was 0.017.

Treated counties had at least $100 (median about $300) of recorded damage per resident, roughly 0.5-1% of annual per-capita income concentrated in one event; a 2% employment difference over four years is within the range found for severe local disasters.
Symmetric to the increases: elasticities of 2-5 imply 4-10% higher imports for a 2 pp cut; 5% is conservative.

Country programmes block dealings with listed parties and deter US counterparties more broadly; a 15% fall in the target's exports to the US relative to its other exports is a moderate effect for programmes that range from narrow listings to near-embargoes.

assumptions: The calibrated noise (unit-specific AR(1) plus cluster-period AR(1) shocks) reproduces the real panels' variance and dependence well enough for the design's standard errors; the calibration check against the real SE tests this and falls back to the analytic MDE when it fails.
The minimum detectable effect is for a homogeneous additive effect; heterogeneous or dynamic effects change power somewhat.
Synthetic panels satisfy parallel trends exactly, so diagnostic failure rates measure how often the checks reject a correct design (their size), not their power against real violations.

Plausible effects were fixed in this registration before any wave-2 outcome was read; the wave-1 ones after wave 1's results were published, and they are stated with sources rather than chosen from those results.

data.inputs: the pinned inputs of each covered design's registration, plus natural_experiment_reports@c7cb3fcd... (wave-1 exposure report, per-storm scores)

outcome_data_examined_before_registratio: Wave-1 outcomes were read by wave 1 and their aggregate results are public (the wave-1 plausible effects above are argued from outside sources, not from those results). No wave-2 outcome had been read when this registration was committed. Calibration reads only untreated cells; the real standard error is read from each design's real panel after that design's own registration was committed.
